_what: Owner decisions the weekly LLM security scan must remember. A finding whose file and vulnerability_type match an entry (case-insensitive regular expressions) is logged and skipped by the issue step, with the reason; it still appears in the uploaded report. Closing an issue in the UI is not a memory the next run can read - this file is. Owner-run CLI tools and vendored code are not listed here: they are excluded from the sweep itself in llm-security-scan.yml.
_how: Add an entry when a finding is a documented design decision, never for one that is merely inconvenient; name the document that carries the reasoning.

accepted.reason: SECURITY.md, 'Data at rest is not encrypted by the app': the Plex token and API keys must be usable by unattended background jobs; encrypting them would only move the key next to the data. Disk encryption is the operator's layer.

SECURITY.md, threat model: Curatarr serves one household over the LAN; TLS and access control belong to the operator's reverse proxy, not to the app. Plex, the *arr services and Ollama are reached by the URLs the owner configured.

Browser code cannot enforce authorization and is not asked to. Verified 2026-09-18 for issue #98: every endpoint it names is gated server-side — /api/setup/reconfigure and /api/setup/build-models by require_admin / require_admin_or_first_run, /api/history/admin/cleanup-orphans and /admin/re-attribute by require_admin, /api/users/me/pin by get_current_user on the caller's own row. SECURITY.md, 'Authorization lives on the routes'.

A service module with no HTTP surface of its own. Verified 2026-09-18 for issue #99: src/routers/setup.py is the only caller and gates every entry point with require_admin or require_admin_or_first_run, plus the first-run setup-code gate (tests/test_setup_hardening.py::test_setup_code_gate_exempts_localhost_and_demands_it_elsewhere).

reset() is deliberately not wired to any route and has zero callers in the tree (verified 2026-09-18 for issue #101, grep over src/ and scripts/). Its docstring carries the rule. An escape hatch an operator can call from a shell is not an exposed endpoint.

A service module with no HTTP surface. Verified 2026-09-21 for issue #114: reattribute_watch_history and cleanup_orphan_watch_history are called only from /api/history/admin/re-attribute and /admin/cleanup-orphans, both behind require_admin; import_plex_history_for_user(user_id) is called only from auth._bootstrap_user_data, which the Plex PIN login schedules with the id of the user row it just created from the PIN exchange — never from a request parameter. SECURITY.md, 'Authorization lives on the routes'.
